Theme

Latin word

vīs

vīs, vīs f.

noun, third declension: accusative vim, ablative vī

a large amount, a mass (with a genitive); violence, assault; power, force; the effect of a thing; force, violence; strength; strength or power

In this lexicon

  • amount

    also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 5.91: magna vīs aurī argentīque

  • assault

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Phil. 2.4: dē vī condemnātī sunt (Lewis & Short s.v. vīs); Traupman 193

  • effect

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Div. 1.73: quod ostentum habuit hanc vim, ut (Lewis & Short); Cic. Div. 2.47: vim et effectum

  • force

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Mil. 9: cum vī vīs illāta dēfenditur (Lewis & Short); Caes. BG 1.14: per vim (Lewis & Short); Traupman 317

  • strength

    the recommended word · classical

  • vīs ēlectrica: electricity

    modern

  • Quid vīs fierī?: what do you expect?

    modern

Examples

  • Sōcratēs, in pompā cum magna vīs aurī argentīque ferrētur, «Quam multa nōn dēsīderō!» inquit.

    When a great amount of gold and silver was being carried in a procession, Socrates said: “How many things I don’t need!”Cic. Tusc. 5.91
